title: How to shoot reference photos for 3D faces

queue.claim: Clinical facial-photography standards use a 90–105 mm (range 85–135 mm) full-frame lens at a fixed distance with the Frankfurt horizontal level (Ettorre et al. 2006; Yavuzer et al. 2001; Galdino et al. 2001). This is the headline default for the lens and distance recommendation.
queue.query: Ettorre 2006 standards for digital photography cranio-maxillo-facial surgery focal length camera distance Frankfurt horizontal

queue.claim: ICAO portrait-quality guidance recommends a camera-to-subject distance of about 1.2–2.5 m and a near-frontal pose within about ±5°, as in ISO/IEC 19794-5 and 39794-5.
queue.query: ICAO portrait quality reference facial images MRTD camera subject distance 1.2 m 2.5 m pose tolerance

queue.claim: Current flagship phone camera focal lengths (35 mm-equivalent): 2× is often a crop of the main sensor (~48–52 mm), 3× is ~65–77 mm, 4–5× is ~100–125 mm. Phones silently switch to a cropped main camera in low light or below the telephoto's minimum focus distance.
queue.query: iPhone 17 Pro telephoto 35mm equivalent focal length minimum focus distance low light switches to main camera crop

queue.claim: Cross-polarised lighting (linear film on the lights plus a lens polariser at 90°) costs about 2–3+ stops of light, and extinction is best for lights near the lens axis.
